key_insight: PWLNet makes neural process surrogates optimization-compatible through exact and piecewise-linear formulations, with pruning improving tractability.
engineering_relevance: Compact neural surrogates can support steady-state operating-point optimization and dynamic reactor control while retaining strong predictive and economic performance.
method: Train baseline or physics-informed networks, then apply optimization-aware pruning.
Embed ReLU, exact tanh, or PWL-tanh models in Pyomo, including binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP formulations.
Use PWL-native training to match training and embedded activations, avoiding extra linearization error.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks, reported results include 6.5× faster MILP solves after 15% pruning on Williams–Otto and 99.7% of direct-shooting reference performance for terminal-aware Van de Vusse prediction.
watch_item: Constraint fidelity needs attention: hydroformylation control slightly exceeded the 20-bar pressure limit, and longer horizons or physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results.
paper_title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
